title: Metamorphic Form In Art
desc:
Although he made his name as a realist painter, in recent years the British artist Clive Head has developed an approach to figurative painting in which images resist a single, stable reading. A form that initially appears to represent one thing may, through sustained looking, reveal itself as something quite different. Figures, objects and spatial relationships can shift in meaning as the viewer moves through the image perceptually, so that the experience of looking becomes active, unstable and extended through time.

In this talk, Head will discuss how these ideas have emerged within his own painting practice and how they relate to broader questions of representation, perception and pictorial structure. He will also consider historical and contemporary artists whose work employs…

title: Junior Dynamics Seminar – Masood Ahmad
desc:
Observable Lyapunov Exponents for Globally Coupled Maps in the Mean-Field Limit

Speaker: Masood Ahmad

Abstract : Large coupled systems can exhibit microscopic chaos alongside stable macroscopic behaviour. We introduce observable Lyapunov exponents to quantify this distinction. For globally coupled maps, we show that these exponents are determined by the linearisation of the self-consistent transfer operator. Applying this result to weakly coupled uniformly expanding maps, we prove that macroscopic perturbations decay near a stationary mean-field state, despite microscopic chaos. Our findings provide a rigorous framework for distinguishing microscopic and macroscopic chaos.

title: Junior Geometry Seminar – Zhengyang Cui
desc:
Title: Blow-ups and Local Integrability

Speaker: Zhengyang Cui

Abstract: For which values of w is |y²-x³|⁻²ʷ integrable near the origin in ℂ²? I will answer this question by resolving the plane cusp y²=x³ and tracking how both the polynomial and the volume form change under each blow-up. The same calculation on a log resolution gives a formula for the critical exponent of an arbitrary complex hypersurface, called its log canonical threshold.

Some snacks will be provided before and after the talk.

Go to the seminar main page.

Subscribe to the mailing list.
venue: Room 140, Huxley Building, South Kensington Campus
